dateAssessment: Working dates use the compatible YAML calendar, April 13–15, 1748. The transcript opens at sunset, crosses two completed nights, and ends with a sunset short rest; it independently establishes the two-day span, not absolute dates. Overnight watches are inferred from eight-hour long rests ending in the morning; storm travel is cumulative, not added again for its nested intervals. The table’s “1230” is a real-world stopping time; the missing constellations do not establish a time jump.

watches.summary: Opening sunset; Vola’s extended dinner conversation ends late in the evening.
Eight-hour overnight rest before an early morning departure; bedtime watch inferred backward from waking.
Midday sun and the raven mark the first travel day.
Evening arrival and camp in the burned plains after the first day’s travel.
Second overnight rest ends at the explicitly narrated next morning; eight hours inferred from long-rest credit.
Arrival around 2–3 p.m.; 1½–2 cumulative storm hours reach late-afternoon light, followed by Delwath’s 20–30-minute reconnaissance.
Sunset and emerging stars during a one-hour short rest.
